jobs.title: Air Quality Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview:

Kimley-Horn's Orange, CA office is seeking an Air Quality Professional with 5+ years of experience specializing in air quality permitting to join our environmental team. The successful candidates will assist in various projects, assisting industrial and municipal clients with their permitting, compliance, and planning needs.

Responsibilities:

* **Technical Support:**
  + Assist in conducting air quality impact assessments, analyses, and dispersion modeling.
  + Perform regulatory and technical analyses in support of permitting project in California and throughout the USA.
  + Familiar with modeling tools and software including CalEEMod, EMFAC, OFFROAD, CALINE4, AERMOD, CAL3QHCR, ISCST3, AERSCREEN, SCREEN3, and GIS.
* **Report Preparation:**
  + Prepare technical reports, environmental impact assessments, and documentation.
  + Conduct air quality impact analyses, health risk assessments, and greenhouse gas analyses.
  + Assist with the preparation of permit applications and compliance documentation.
* **Field Work:**
  + Participate in field studies and data collection activities related to air quality.
  + Participate in compliance audits for environmental topics including air pollutants, toxics, hazardous materials, etc.
* **Data Analysis:**
  + Perform emission calculations for various industrial processes.
  + Understanding design documents and engineering drawings.
  + Utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other relevant software for environmental analysis.

Qualifications:

* Degree (Bachelors or Masters) in Environmental Science, engineering (environmental, chemical, mechanical, civil), atmospheric sciences, physics, chemistry, data science or related field
* 5+ years of experience in environmental consulting, with a focus on air quality permitting
* Certified Permitting Professional (CPP) a plus
* Experience with data centers and power production
* Strong understanding of environmental laws, regulations, and standards (e.g., Clean Air Act, CEQA).
* Strong writing/verbal skills
* Working knowledge of GIS/ArcView
* Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills
* Positive attitude and a strong work ethic
* Strong sense of urgency and self-initiative to meet client deadlines
* Detail-oriented team player with an ability to contribute to a positive work environment
* Ability to work independently and as a team

**Salary Range**: $90,000 - $125,000

Why Kimley-Horn?:

At Kimley-Horn, we do things differently. People, clients, and employees are at the forefront of who we are. Clients know we prioritize achieving their goals and growing their success. Employees know our culture and approach to business are built on a desire to provide an environment for everyone to flourish. Our commitment to quality is only as good as the people behind it— that’s why we welcome and develop passionate, hardworking, and proactive employees. We take pride in how our employee retention, robust benefits package, and company values have led to Kimley-Horn’s placement on the Fortune “100 Best Companies to Work” list for 19 years!

*Key Benefits at Kimley-Horn*

* Exceptional Retirement Plan: 2-to1- company match on up to 4% of eligible compensation (salary + bonus) and additional profit-sharing contribution.
* Comprehensive Health Coverage: Low-cost medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
* Time Off: Personal leave, flexible scheduling, floating holidays, and half-day Fridays.
* Financial Wellness: Student loan matching in our 401(k), and performance-based bonuses.
* Professional Development: Tuition reimbursement and extensive internal training programs.
* Family-Friendly Benefits: New Parent Leave, family building benefits, and childcare resources.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking to use your mix of field and analytical skills to recover endangered Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep? The Department of Fish and Wildlife is seeking a motivated individual to work as an Environmental Scientist in the Sierra Bighorn Recovery Program.
  
  
The position will focus on Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep but will also include work on their predators. Data collection will include field work such as helicopter and ground surveys (hiking and backpacking). The incumbent will be responsible for wildlife management and analysis of large spatial and demographic datasets; excellent R coding is essential.

The incumbent will run Bayesian integrated population models that use estimates of abundance, vital rates, and spatial data for Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep. Participate in captures to deploy GPS collars, collect nutritional data using ultrasonography, conduct disease surveillance and genetic sampling. Use GIS and statistical methods to inform reintroduction efforts. Conduct, and analyze threats to the recovery of Sierra bighorn. Analyze large scale climate data to project and interpret its effects on Sierra bighorn recovery. Analyze environmental, habitat, and predation threats that influence progress towards recovery goals. The incumbent will also assist in maintaining consumptive and non-consumptive uses of wildlife.  
  
  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

Environmental Scientist: Exam Bulletin Link

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Must be able to work in various habitats including but not limited to high altitudes (8,000 – 14,000 feet), arid environments and valley, grassland, conifer and riparian habitats, in inclement weather, and in rugged backcountry terrain during all months of the year. This position will require wildlife restraint certification to chemically immobilize animals. Travel up to 40% multiple nights for fieldwork and will attend meetings and conferences as directed. This position offers the possibility of an office-centered telework agreement based on the Department's current Telework Policy. As a condition of employment, the incumbent may be required to wear an appropriate uniform consistent with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901) for various work situations, including field surveys and public interaction, both within and outside the Region as required by the supervisor.

Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) employees are committed to managing and protecting California’s diverse wildlife and the habitats upon which they depend.

  

California is one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. As such, CDFW values diverse employees working together to protect nature for all Californians. CDFW is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where all backgrounds, cultures and personal experiences can thrive and connect others to our critical mission.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under close or general direction of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) in the Local Enforcement Agency (LEA) Evaluation Unit, the Environmental Scientist (ES) will implement the LEA certification program, the LEA, and Tire Enforcement Agency (TEA) evaluation programs, and matters associated with LEA/TEA performance evaluation outcomes related to solid waste/waste tire program implementation. The incumbent will apply basic principles of chemistry, biology, physical and environmental sciences, environmental characteristics of waste materials and solid waste systems related to public health and environmental protection standards. The ES will be required to gather complex data from multiple sources, review, analyze and assess compliance in the areas of solid waste facility permitting, inspection, closure and maintenance of LEA/TEA program requirements and records. The ES will communicate with all levels of local government and CalRecycle management, regarding LEA/TEA evaluation findings, action items and program recommendations necessary to certify an LEA or to bring LEA/TEA programs in line with statutes and regulations. The incumbent will participate in forums, workgroups, and special projects within CalRecycle as related to the LEA Evaluation Unit, Tire Enforcement Section, Financial Resources Section and CalRecycle’s overall priorities. The incumbent may be required to travel as part of this position, with duration and time variant upon meeting and facility locations.

**As of July 1st, 2026, the position is office-centered, and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code section 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting eligibility set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location in Sacramento, at their own expense. The EPA headquarters building offices in downtown Sacramento are well-lit, enclosed, non-windowed office cubicles in a smoke-free environment.

The 40-hour work week schedule is typically dayshift, Monday through Friday. Office and field work includes, on a regular basis, writing and reviewing inspection reports and notices, contact with the regulated community by way of in-person, phone and video conferencing, preparation and review of other documents and internet research. Overnight travel may be required locally and within the state. The job occasionally requires you to perform field inspections, hear vehicles and alarms or other audible signals of possible risk.

jobs.title: Utah Watershed Restoration & Partnerships Manager
jobs.description:
This is a remote position that must be based in Utah's Greater Salt Lake region (e.g., Salt Lake City, Ogden, Logan, Park City, Heber City, or Provo).

**About the Program**

WRI's U.S. Forests and Water program, part of the global Cities4Forests initiative, works to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire, restore degraded forests, and protect watersheds across the U.S. The program focuses on designing, implementing, financing, and scaling projects with local partners to build disaster resilience, strengthen water security, protect and enhance infrastructure, create jobs and recreation opportunities, and boost rural prosperity.

In Utah, WRI has served as a strategic partner for the U.S. Forest Service, water and electric utilities, state agencies, conservation organizations, academia, and local governments for nearly a decade and has worked to improve watershed health and reduce wildfire risk across the Great Salt Lake Basin. A key component of this work is the Utah Resilience Fund, an innovative fund that brings together public, private, and philanthropic funding to scale watershed restoration and long-term resilience. Additional information on the U.S. project portfolio can be found here.

**Job Highlight**

The Utah Watershed Restoration Manager will help advance watershed restoration, partnerships, and resilience projects across Utah, with an initial emphasis on the Jordan River watershed and its forested source watersheds. This position is focused on developing a pipeline of restoration projects from planning to implementation by coordinating partners, advancing policy priorities, supporting funding acquisition, and helping deliver on-the-ground restoration outcomes at scale.

Working closely with the Utah Watershed Resilience Manager, Research & Project Development Manager, Cities4Forests' senior leadership and a diverse network of local partners, the Manager will build and maintain relationships with municipalities, water providers, conservation districts, state and federal agencies, community organizations, and other stakeholders. The role will help identify restoration opportunities, remove implementation barriers, navigate policy and permitting processes, secure project funding, and support successful project delivery.

The successful candidate brings a strong understanding of Utah's water, watershed, forest, and wildfire landscape, an established network of relationships within the Greater Salt Lake region, and experience coordinating complex environmental or infrastructure projects. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys working directly with communities and partners to turn plans into action and create measurable benefits for watersheds, communities, and ecosystems.

**What You Will Do**

**Restoration Planning & Watershed Leadership (40%)**

  

* Lead planning, implementation, and scaling of watershed restoration and resilience projects across priority watersheds, with an initial focus on the Jordan River watershed and Greater Salt Lake Basin.
* Partner with utilities, local governments, agencies, NGOs, and land managers to identify, prioritize, and advance restoration projects that improve watershed health, water security, and wildfire resilience.
* Help utilities consider financing approaches for integrated grey and green infrastructure strategies.
* Help move projects from concept to implementation by supporting project development, permitting, funding, stakeholder coordination, and delivery across public and private lands.
* Support development of near- and long-term restoration strategies informed by watershed science, wildfire risk, partner priorities, and implementation readiness.
* Track project performance, budgets, and outcomes, and support monitoring and evaluation efforts.

**Partnership Building & Policy Engagement (40%)**

  

* Build trusted relationships with utilities, local governments, conservation organizations, state and federal agencies, community groups, and other partners.
* Lead watershed collaboratives, technical committees, and partner working groups to align priorities and accelerate restoration outcomes.
* Monitor and participate in water, forestry, wildfire, and watershed policy discussions relevant to WRI's work and restoration goals.
* Identify opportunities to align restoration priorities with local, state, and federal programs and funding sources.
* Develop recommendations and strategies that remove barriers to implementation and increase investment in watershed resilience.

**Fundraising, Communications & Outreach (20%)**

  

* Lead the drafting of grant proposals and funding applications to support the work in Utah.
* Develop and steward opportunities and relationships with current and prospective donors.
* Represent WRI and the Utah Resilience Fund at conferences, workshops, utility meetings, and stakeholder events.
* Develop presentations, reports, case studies, and communications materials highlighting project impacts and lessons learned.
* Support peer learning among Utah partners and national watershed programs.
* Support efforts to position Utah as a national leader in watershed resilience and conservation finance.
* Contribute to publications, blogs, webinars, and other outreach activities that share best practices and elevate project visibility.

**What You Will Need**

**Experience**

* Master's degree in natural resources, environmental policy, water resources, forestry, planning, public administration, or a related field. Work experience can be substituted in lieu of a degree.
* Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience.
* Demonstrated experience implementing natural resource, watershed, water, forestry, wildfire, or environmental restoration projects.
* Experience working with local governments, utilities, conservation organizations, state agencies, federal agencies, or watershed partnerships.
* Experience navigating public processes, permitting, grants, policy development, or interagency coordination.
